variants.name: pthread mutex + condition variable result slot (hand-written future)
variants.idiom_name: pthread_mutex_t + pthread_cond_t guarded once-only result slot
variants.implementation_notes: POSIX supplies only the pieces: a once-only slot - a struct holding a state flag plus the value or the error - protected by a pthread_mutex_t, with a pthread_cond_t to publish readiness and pthread_cond_timedwait for a deadline-carrying wait. The producer runs on a thread or work-queue worker, stores its result while holding the mutex and signals; the consumer's read end is an explicit wait loop over the predicate, because C has no async/await to replace it with. Keep the blocking form when the surrounding code is thread-based; inside an existing event loop the completion-callback variant is the better fit.
pitfalls: A lost wake-up or a producer that exits without publishing parks the waiter forever: set the state while holding the mutex, signal after unlocking, and always re-test the predicate in a loop because the wait can return spuriously.
The slot's lifetime is manual: freeing a future a waiter still holds, or pointing it at a producer's stack frame, is a use-after-free - tie the storage to the consumer or reference-count it.

variants.name: libuv thread-pool completion callback (event-loop future)
variants.idiom_name: uv_queue_work + after-work callback on the libuv loop
variants.implementation_notes: In an event-driven program the same handoff becomes a completion callback: uv_queue_work runs the blocking computation on libuv's thread pool and invokes the after-work callback back on the loop, which is the value-is-ready notification - the continuations live in the loop's design rather than in a wait loop. The pending value is the work request plus its result slot, the promise side is the code that fills that slot, and the read end is the callback registration; choose it when the process already owns a libuv loop and no thread may block.
pitfalls: The completion callback runs on the loop thread, so anything slow inside it stalls every other handle - hand heavy follow-up work back to the pool or to a queue.
The work request and its result slot must outlive the pool job: freeing them in the submit path is the classic use-after-free, and blocking the loop while waiting for the result defeats the design.
